fields.detail: Directive 3: gsplit_line.py tested only ONE bipartition (even- vs odd-index blocks) and found it not strictly line-separable — a dead guess, not an obstruction. The question that bears on the induction f(n) <= 2*f(n-1): does ANY line (containing no point) split the verified es_construct set into two halves each free of a convex (n-1)-gon? Decide exhaustively at n=5,6,7. Method: every combinatorially distinct half-plane bipartition of a finite planar set is realized by a line through a pair of points (standard k-set fact), so enumerate the C(N,2) point pairs, the line through each pair, and the 4 perturbations assigning the two on-line points to either side — that covers every bipartition. For each: both sides must have exactly 2^{n-3} points and no convex (n-1)-subset (exact es_geom oracle, integer determinants). Report the exact count of distinct bipartitions tried and of valid splits, and state what an empty result rules out. If no line exists, record the negative in CONTEXT.md under Ruled out with scope exactly 'this es_construct realization at n=5,6,7', NOT all extremal sets, and update the G-split-consistent gap in research/backward/extremal-split-stability.md. A pattern is worth finding only if the quantity it is a pattern in is defined for EVERY n-avoiding set of size 2^{n-2}, not for this one. Examples that qualify: the convex-position spectrum of the known 32-point record set compared against es_construct at the same N, order-type invariants that survive re-realization, any statistic computable on two non-isomorphic n-avoiding sets and compared. If a quantity cannot be computed on a second set, it is not a pattern, it is a coordinate — do not file it. Then WORK THE TWO QUEUED TASKS (lift-or-declare-strongest-template-fact; nullstellensatz-grid-first-target). Do NOT claim the conjecture proved.
fields.title: pattern_finder: no more es_construct spectra; patterns must be computable on a second set (directive 22)

fields.detail: Directive 23: 'Fetch the Aichholzer order-type database if reachable — the second family is what makes these liftable. That is a fetch, not a sweep.' ONE fetch of the Aichholzer order-type database (small n, up to ~10) as the second family for the convex-4set-supersaturation and layer-transfer-matrix lifts. If unreachable, say so and continue with the Karolyi–Toth twin as the only second family. Do NOT turn this into a reading/exa session. Capture the source URL beside whatever it yields.
fields.title: Fetch the Aichholzer order-type database if reachable (directive 23) — a fetch, not a sweep

fields.detail: Directive 23 item 3. Realize es_construct(n) n=5,6,7; compute the polar dual line arrangement by EXACT rational duality of the verified es_geom point set; with q outside, compute the level profile and face counts of q's cell. Verify the primal convex-position oracle against the dual convex-q-cell criterion on all subsets up to n=6 exhaustively. Worth having whatever the approach does. Falsifier to hunt first: the dual of some 2^{n-2}+1-point set whose q-cell is concave in a way Euler/level cannot exclude — i.e. the arrangement counting gives only a >=4^n bound (record that plainly; it is the known loss recurring). Capture with AGENTS.md command+EXIT idiom. Report numbers, not readings.
fields.title: Run polar-arrangement-euler-levels first step: exact rational dual of es_construct, verify primal vs dual convex-q-cell to n=6 (directive 23)

fields.detail: Directive 23 item 2. On the verified onion layers of es_construct at n=5,6,7, exact determinants: for every pair of consecutive onion layers and every pair a,b in the outer layer, count how many inner-layer points lie in the forward cone a->b. Check whether per-layer capacity is uniformly <= (n-2 - chain length) with equality the extremal signature, and whether the DP reproduces 2^{n-2} on es_construct. THEN run the SAME DP on the Karolyi–Toth twin construction (held) — the second family is the point; a capacity bound holding only on es_construct is another coordinate. Optionally compare against Aichholzer order types once the aichholzer-fetch task lands. Falsifier: a no-convex-n-gon set of size 2^{n-2} whose layers violate the cone-capacity bound. Capture with command+EXIT. Report numbers, not readings.
fields.title: Run layer-transfer-matrix first step: cross-layer cone capacities, es_construct then Karolyi–Toth twin (directive 23)

fields.detail: Directive 23 item 1, the cheapest sharpest falsifier, run FIRST. Count the non-convex 4-subsets NNC(N) exactly on es_construct at n=5,6,7 (N=2^{n-2} = 8,16,32) and test the covering bound NNC(N) * C(N-4,n-4) >= C(N,n) at N=2^{n-2}, and whether it strictly fails at N=2^{n-2}+1. It either holds at the extremal and fails one larger, or it does not. Exact determinants against the verified lib.es_geom. Then lift to the second family: the same count on the Karolyi–Toth twin and on Aichholzer order types up to n<=10 (see aichholzer-fetch). Falsifier to hunt first: an n-avoiding set on 2^{n-2} points whose covering ratio is significantly smaller than es_construct — the bound then fails transparently. Capture with AGENTS.md command+EXIT. Report numbers, not readings. Do NOT claim the conjecture proved.
fields.title: Run convex-4set-supersaturation first step: exact NNC(N) on es_construct + covering-ratio test (directive 23 item 1)
